items.title: 2028-29 school calendar, comment before the 22 Sep board vote
items.detail: Optional. LCPS reopened comment because board members proposed revisions and new options since the last round. The School Board votes Tuesday 22 Sep. There is a Let's Talk form that sends comments straight to the members. Adi would be in 8th grade that year.

items.title: Intramurals and after school clubs start this week
items.detail: Posted to the Grade 6 course on Monday morning by Kjersti Oliver. Any day she stays after school she has to fill in the After School Attendance Form herself, once per day. Pickup is either a parent run or one of the two 5:00 pm activity buses, and the bus number and stop are on the 2026-2027 activity bus route sheet. Worth settling which bus she is on before the first day she stays.

items.title: Mr. Dickerson weekly update, content is in the attached PDF
items.detail: US History weekly note sent Sunday, running a week behind by his own admission. The email body is empty and everything sits in an attached PDF named 9-7-26.pdf, so it covers the week of 7 Sep rather than the current one. Open it from the email if you want the detail.

items.title: Substance abuse presentation in PE, opt out form attached
items.detail: Mrs. Allen wrote on 11 Sep that all sixth graders sit a Substance Abuse Presentation on 27 or 28 October during their normal PE period. An opt out document is attached to her email, so the decision is yours and the form goes back to her. No deadline was given, which usually means before the week of the presentation. Worth opening the attachment now rather than in late October.

items.title: Our Turn to Talk, parent and teen film night, 24 Sep
items.detail: Optional. A film following five teenagers on mental health and growing up, then a facilitated discussion. Thursday 24 Sep, 6 to 8 pm at the LCPS Administration Building in Ashburn. Food at 6, film at 6:30. Recommended for ages 12 and up, so she is on the edge of it. Registration required.

items.title: Gifted evaluation window, probably not needed for her
items.detail: LCPS opened the fall evaluation cycle for grades 6 to 8. The Permission to Evaluate form is due Friday 25 Sep and late forms are refused, though sixth and seventh graders get another cycle in January 2027. She is already scheduled in Spectrum 6 with Mrs. Cumberledge, which is the identified gifted programme, so this almost certainly does not apply to her. One question to the school gifted resource teacher settles it. Form link sits on the LCPS Gifted and Talented page.

items.title: New teacher messaging app, Rooms by Apptegy
items.detail: LCPS launched a two way messaging tool this year. It becomes the only channel for quick notes from teachers, coaches and activity leaders. Invitations went out 2 Sep by text or email and will be resent next week, but you can join without one. Download the LCPS app, allow notifications, pick Watson Mountain in the Feed tab, then use the Rooms or Messaging tab at the bottom. Schoology still holds assignments and ParentVUE still holds grades.

items.title: FY28 budget ThoughtExchange closes 15 Sep
items.detail: Optional. The School Board is collecting parent input on programs and investments for the 2027 to 2028 year, with slower revenue growth expected. Open at lcps.org/thoughtexchange.

items.title: Video Game Music Club, she is not eligible yet
items.detail: Runs Wednesdays after school, led by Mr. Klinberg. Sixth graders need at least one full year of playing plus permission from Ms. Holowecki, so this is a no for now. Ms. Holowecki is starting a Beginning Strings Club for beginners in the second club season and will send details as the first season closes. Fee carries an extra $15 that pays the professional guest musicians.

items.title: Fall club registration has already closed
items.detail: Registration opened to all families Sunday 6 Sep at 10:00 am and closed Monday 7 Sep. Several clubs sold out during PTO priority access before that. Bus transport was offered for PM sessions only. Year long clubs are separate and the PTO says details are still coming, so that is the next window to watch. Club questions go to clubs@watsonmountainpto.org.

items.title: Math homework runs on Mathspace, most nights
items.detail: Mrs. Reel expects homework after most classes, due the following class period, mostly on Mathspace. Every unit also has a Schoology folder with an agenda listing each day, assignments, completed notes and upcoming test dates. That agenda is the first place to look after an absence.

scans.summary: Two day scan, pushed late because the previous token stopped authenticating. English 6H loaded a full unit in one go: an in class formative on point of view, conflict and theme today, a compare and contrast tracker due Friday 18 Sep, and the first major summative of the quarter, a one pager poster, due Wednesday 30 Sep. The poster is the thing to plan around. Spectrum 6 Field Methods is marked submitted on the basis that it left the upcoming list after the 4:00 pm cutoff without appearing as overdue, and no score has posted. Added the 2028-29 calendar comment window, which closes with the board vote on 22 Sep. No new grades. Eight Peachjar flyers, all eighth grade or Academies events, nothing that applies.

Two day scan. Two new scores: Math 7 integer operations review from 10 Sep came back 98 out of 100, her first mark under full credit this year, and the PE Week 4 Ultimate Football participation credit posted 20 out of 20 this morning. Added the notice that intramurals and after school clubs start this week, which carries a daily attendance form she fills in herself and a choice between a parent pickup and the two 5:00 pm activity buses. Mr. Dickerson sent his weekly US History update on Sunday with an empty body and everything inside a PDF dated 7 Sep, so it is logged as a pointer rather than pulled apart. No overdue submissions. Spectrum 6 Field Methods is still the only thing due this week, tomorrow at 4:00 pm.

Two day scan. Both outstanding scores landed: the Science 6H OIP quiz came back 100 out of 100 on 11 Sep and the English 6H Vocab Unit 1 test came back 100 out of 100 on the evening of 10 Sep. Both moved off the coursework board and onto the grades list. Nothing else changed. No overdue submissions, no new assignments, and the only thing ahead in the next week is the Spectrum 6 Field Methods task at 4:00 pm on Tuesday 15 Sep. The 12 Sep Mountain Messenger was image only with no extractable text, so nothing came out of it.

RSM pass. Lesson 1 homework is done and scored 100 out of 100, confirmed by the Ashburn office on 9 Sep and repeated on the 11 Sep weekly update, so it is marked complete and the score is on the grades list. Lesson 2 homework was assigned this morning for the current week and is now on the board against next Thursday, 17 Sep, since RSM gave no explicit deadline. Written solutions still go to class either way.

Five day scan. One genuinely new action: Mrs. Allen sent the sixth grade substance abuse presentation notice on 11 Sep with an opt out document attached, presentation on 27 or 28 October in PE. Added the 24 Sep Our Turn to Talk film night as optional. Yom Kippur on 21 Sep is already on the calendar so nothing changed there. No new grades and no new assignments beyond what was already listed; the OIP quiz and the Vocab Unit 1 test are both still submitted and unscored. A late bus alert went out for B2038 on the morning of 9 Sep and has since cleared.

Brightened the subject washes to roughly twice the saturation and widened the left spine to 5px so it still reads against the stronger colour. Math sits a shade lighter than the rest because full brightness dropped it to 4.43 contrast against the orange, below the floor.

Colour pass, no mail scan. Every block in the day schedule now carries a pastel wash in its subject colour with a solid spine on the left edge, the block number and time take the subject colour, class names on Coursework and Grades became pastel pills, and the block map legend matches. Contrast checked on all nine subjects, weakest is Math at 4.83 against its wash. Print sheet untouched.
Removed the math notebook check from the standing jobs at your request. The Art 6 supply list from Ms. Thiele is now the only open item in What to do.

Page changes, no new mail. Due times now show on the card, so the Spectrum task reads 4:00 pm rather than just Tuesday. Work she has handed in but that is not graded stays on the board for three days marked submitted, instead of vanishing. Task rows carry a link straight to Schoology. Mathspace and Rooms added to the quick links, a bus line added under the header, and a quarter end countdown appears inside 30 days. Coursework text is now escaped like everywhere else, the holiday calendar is written once instead of three times, and the script moved out to app.js so the file can be pushed normally again.

Good day. The overdue Histograms task came back 100/100, so it was submitted and it cost nothing. PE Procedures and Rules major summative also posted 100/100. Both of yesterday's deadlines are closed: Vocab Unit 1 test submitted at 12:02 pm and the Science OIP quiz at 2:56 pm, neither graded yet. One new item, a Spectrum 6 Field Methods task due Tuesday 15 Sep at 4:00 pm, which is an afternoon deadline rather than the usual midnight. Nothing left on the list until then. RSM is tonight at 6:20 with Lesson 1 homework due. Yom Kippur on Monday 21 Sep is a student holiday and was already on the calendar. Still open: math notebook check, shoulder rest, and the Art 6 supply list from Ms. Thiele.
